title: A GTK4 ssh-askpass in Zig
excerpt: Every ssh-askpass in the _Gentoo_ tree pulls in _X11_ or a full _KDE_ stack, so I wrote my own with _Zig_ 0.16 and _GTK4_, with hand-written bindings that keep `X` out of the build.
content_html:
Every ssh-askpass in the Gentoo tree pulls in X11 or a full KDE stack, so I wrote my own with Zig 0.16 and GTK4, with hand-written bindings that keep X out of the build.

I run hardened Gentoo on my laptop, and most of the time I never touch ssh-askpass because I’m using -sk keys for most of the systems. There is one class of situation where I do need it, though, which is when a program wants an SSH key passphrase for a regular ED25519 key, but has no terminal to read it from. The usual case is go get, or the go toolchain in general, fetching a private module over SSH during a build that runs without a TTY. OpenSSH can’t prompt on a pipe, so it runs whatever SSH_ASKPASS points at and puts the passphrase prompt in a window instead. For years I had nothing installed for that and had to work around these scenarios. The main reason for that is what Gentoo’s Portage offers:

This is where I gave up on the packaged options. Even setting the X11 question aside, every one of these uses GTK2 or GTK3 at most. However, it just so happened that I had wanted to build something with GTK4 for a long time, so instead of patching one of the existing implementations, which are mostly C anyway, I wrote my own with Zig 0.16 and GTK4, and called it ssh-askpass-zigtk.

Avoiding X11

The reason the GTK helpers break on my system is the headers. The standard way of calling GTK includes the GTK4 headers, which pull in GDK, and GDK still ships gdk/gdkx.h on most installs, so an X11 header comes in whether you want it or not. Zig’s @cImport, the obvious way to call a C library, would do the same, because it pulls in exactly those headers. So ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t @cImport anything. src/gtk.zig declares the thirty-odd GTK and GLib functions the program calls by hand, as plain extern prototypes:

pub const Widget = opaque {};

pub extern fn gtk_window_new() *Widget;
pub extern fn gtk_password_entry_new() *Widget;
pub extern fn gtk_editable_get_text(editable: *Widget) [*:0]const u8;
pub extern fn gtk_button_new_with_label(label: [*:0]const u8) *Widget;

Nothing in that file names a symbol from gdk/gdkx.h or X11/Xlib.h, so the compiler never sees an X header, and the binary builds and runs against a GTK4 that was compiled without X11. The one X-adjacent value it needs, the Escape keysym, is hardcoded as 0xff1b rather than pulled from gdk/gdkkeysyms.h.

GTK is built on GObject, which does single inheritance by putting the parent struct as the first member of the child, so a window, a box, a label, a password entry and a button are all layout-compatible with a GtkWidget * at the ABI boundary. On the Zig side one opaque {} type stands in for all of them, and every widget function takes and returns the same *Widget, without a hierarchy of wrapper types to model something the C ABI already flattens.

The parts that don’t touch GTK, the mapping of SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT to a dialog type and the parsing of the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR variables, are in src/root.zig with unit tests, so they run under zig build test with no display and no GTK at all. Recoloring goes through a small CSS provider, since GTK4 removed gtk_widget_modify_fg and _bg.

Cross-compiling

Because the bindings are hand-written externs and no GTK headers enter the build, Zig can cross-compile the binary for any Linux architecture without a GTK4 toolchain for that target. The only thing missing at link time is the GTK4 shared library itself, and -Dgtk-stub covers that, as it builds a tiny stub libgtk-4.so.1 whose exported symbols are all no-ops, links the executable against that, and lets the target’s real GTK4 resolve at runtime instead. The release workflow uses this to produce binaries for x86_64, aarch64, armv7, riscv64, powerpc64le, i386, loongarch64 and s390x from one machine, none of which has GTK4 installed for the other seven.

Note: ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t grab the keyboard as other askpass implementations normally would. The GTK3 helper calls gdk_seat_grab so another client can’t read the passphrase as you type it, but from what I see, GTK4 dropped that interface and I believe that Wayland doesn’t let a client grab the keyboard at all, so there is no portable way to do it without X11. Hence the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER and GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER variables also have no effect.

The code is on tty.fail and mirrored to GitHub, where each tagged release ships prebuilt Linux binaries per architecture. To use it, put the binary somewhere on your PATH and point SSH_ASKPASS at it. For a terminal that means two lines in ~/.profile or your shell’s startup file (e.g. ~/.zshrc for my fellow Zsh users):

export SSH_ASKPASS=~/.local/bin/ssh-askpass-zigtk
export SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer

SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer, from OpenSSH 8.4 onward, tells OpenSSH to use the dialog even when a terminal is available, as long as a graphical session is present. On a systemd user session, the same two variables go in ~/.config/environment.d/ssh-askpass.conf as plain KEY=VALUE lines with an absolute path, since that file neither expands ~ nor runs a shell. Log out and back in, and the next ssh-add, git pull or go get that needs a passphrase without a terminal gets the dialog.

Even setting the X11 question aside, every one of these uses GTK2 or GTK3 at most. However, it just so happened that I had wanted to build something with GTK4 for a long time, so instead of patching one of the existing implementations, which are mostly C anyway, I wrote my own with Zig 0.16 and GTK4, and called it ssh-askpass-zigtk.Avoiding X11The reason the GTK helpers break on my system is the headers. The standard way of calling GTK includes the GTK4 headers, which pull in GDK, and GDK still ships gdk/gdkx.h on most installs, so an X11 header comes in whether you want it or not. Zig’s @cImport, the obvious way to call a C library, would do the same, because it pulls in exactly those headers. So ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t @cImport anything. src/gtk.zig declares the thirty-odd GTK and GLib functions the program calls by hand, as plain extern prototypes:pub const Widget = opaque {}; pub extern fn gtk_window_new() *Widget; pub extern fn gtk_password_entry_new() *Widget; pub extern fn gtk_editable_get_text(editable: *Widget) [*:0]const u8; pub extern fn gtk_button_new_with_label(label: [*:0]const u8) *Widget; Nothing in that file names a symbol from gdk/gdkx.h or X11/Xlib.h, so the compiler never sees an X header, and the binary builds and runs against a GTK4 that was compiled without X11. The one X-adjacent value it needs, the Escape keysym, is hardcoded as 0xff1b rather than pulled from gdk/gdkkeysyms.h.GTK is built on GObject, which does single inheritance by putting the parent struct as the first member of the child, so a window, a box, a label, a password entry and a button are all layout-compatible with a GtkWidget * at the ABI boundary. On the Zig side one opaque {} type stands in for all of them, and every widget function takes and returns the same *Widget, without a hierarchy of wrapper types to model something the C ABI already flattens.The parts that don’t touch GTK, the mapping of SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT to a dialog type and the parsing of the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR variables, are in src/root.zig with unit tests, so they run under zig build test with no display and no GTK at all. Recoloring goes through a small CSS provider, since GTK4 removed gtk_widget_modify_fg and _bg.Cross-compilingBecause the bindings are hand-written externs and no GTK headers enter the build, Zig can cross-compile the binary for any Linux architecture without a GTK4 toolchain for that target. The only thing missing at link time is the GTK4 shared library itself, and -Dgtk-stub covers that, as it builds a tiny stub libgtk-4.so.1 whose exported symbols are all no-ops, links the executable against that, and lets the target’s real GTK4 resolve at runtime instead. The release workflow uses this to produce binaries for x86_64, aarch64, armv7, riscv64, powerpc64le, i386, loongarch64 and s390x from one machine, none of which has GTK4 installed for the other seven.Note: ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t grab the keyboard as other askpass implementations normally would. The GTK3 helper calls gdk_seat_grab so another client can’t read the passphrase as you type it, but from what I see, GTK4 dropped that interface and I believe that Wayland doesn’t let a client grab the keyboard at all, so there is no portable way to do it without X11. Hence the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER and GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER variables also have no effect.The code is on tty.fail and mirrored to GitHub, where each tagged release ships prebuilt Linux binaries per architecture. To use it, put the binary somewhere on your PATH and point SSH_ASKPASS at it. For a terminal that means two lines in ~/.profile or your shell’s startup file (e.g. ~/.zshrc for my fellow Zsh users):export SSH_ASKPASS=~/.local/bin/ssh-askpass-zigtk export SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer, from OpenSSH 8.4 onward, tells OpenSSH to use the dialog even when a terminal is available, as long as a graphical session is present. On a systemd user session, the same two variables go in ~/.config/environment.d/ssh-askpass.conf as plain KEY=VALUE lines with an absolute path, since that file neither expands ~ nor runs a shell. Log out and back in, and the next ssh-add, git pull or go get that needs a passphrase without a terminal gets the dialog.

sentences.en: Avoiding X11

blocks.html_en: The reason the GTK helpers break on my system is the headers. The standard way of calling GTK includes the GTK4 headers, which pull in GDK, and GDK still ships gdk/gdkx.h on most installs, so an X11 header comes in whether you want it or not. Zig’s @cImport, the obvious way to call a C library, would do the same, because it pulls in exactly those headers. So ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t @cImport anything. src/gtk.zig declares the thirty-odd GTK and GLib functions the program calls by hand, as plain extern prototypes:

sentences.zh: GTK 帮助程序在我的系统上崩溃的原因是标头。

sentences.en: So ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t @cImport anything.

sentences.en: The one X-adjacent value it needs, the Escape keysym, is hardcoded as 0xff1b rather than pulled from gdk/gdkkeysyms.h.
sentences.zh: 它需要的一个 X 相邻值（Escape 键符号）被硬编码为 0xff1b，而不是从 gdk/gdkkeysyms.h 中提取。

blocks.html_en: GTK is built on GObject, which does single inheritance by putting the parent struct as the first member of the child, so a window, a box, a label, a password entry and a button are all layout-compatible with a GtkWidget * at the ABI boundary. On the Zig side one opaque {} type stands in for all of them, and every widget function takes and returns the same *Widget, without a hierarchy of wrapper types to model something the C ABI already flattens.

sentences.en: GTK is built on GObject, which does single inheritance by putting the parent struct as the first member of the child, so a window, a box, a label, a password entry and a button are all layout-compatible with a GtkWidget * at the ABI boundary.
sentences.zh: GTK 构建于 GObject 之上，它通过将父结构体作为子结构体的第一个成员来实现单继承，因此窗口、框、标签、密码条目和按钮都与 ABI 边界处的 GtkWidget * 布局兼容。

sentences.en: On the Zig side one opaque {} type stands in for all of them, and every widget function takes and returns the same *Widget, without a hierarchy of wrapper types to model something the C ABI already flattens.
sentences.zh: 在 Zig 方面，一个不透明的 {} 类型代表所有这些，并且每个 widget 函数都接受并返回相同的 *Widget，没有包装器类型的层次结构来对 C ABI 已经扁平化的东西进行建模。

blocks.html_en: The parts that don’t touch GTK, the mapping of SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT to a dialog type and the parsing of the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR variables, are in src/root.zig with unit tests, so they run under zig build test with no display and no GTK at all. Recoloring goes through a small CSS provider, since GTK4 removed gtk_widget_modify_fg and _bg.

sentences.en: The parts that don’t touch GTK, the mapping of SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT to a dialog type and the parsing of the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR variables, are in src/root.zig with unit tests, so they run under zig build test with no display and no GTK at all.
sentences.zh: 不涉及 GTK 的部分，即 SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT 到对话框类型的映射以及 GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR 变量的解析，位于 src/root.zig 中并进行了单元测试，因此它们在 zig 构建测试下运行，没有显示，也根本没有 GTK。

sentences.en: Recoloring goes through a small CSS provider, since GTK4 removed gtk_widget_modify_fg and _bg.
sentences.zh: 由于 GTK4 删除了 gtk_widget_modify_fg 和 _bg，因此重新着色需要通过一个小型 CSS 提供程序。

sentences.en: Cross-compiling
sentences.zh: 交叉编译

blocks.html_en: Because the bindings are hand-written externs and no GTK headers enter the build, Zig can cross-compile the binary for any Linux architecture without a GTK4 toolchain for that target. The only thing missing at link time is the GTK4 shared library itself, and -Dgtk-stub covers that, as it builds a tiny stub libgtk-4.so.1 whose exported symbols are all no-ops, links the executable against that, and lets the target’s real GTK4 resolve at runtime instead. The release workflow uses this to produce binaries for x86_64, aarch64, armv7, riscv64, powerpc64le, i386, loongarch64 and s390x from one machine, none of which has GTK4 installed for the other seven.

sentences.en: Because the bindings are hand-written externs and no GTK headers enter the build, Zig can cross-compile the binary for any Linux architecture without a GTK4 toolchain for that target.
sentences.zh: 由于绑定是手写的 extern，并且没有 GTK 标头进入构建，因此 Zig 可以为任何 Linux 架构交叉编译二进制文件，而无需该目标的 GTK4 工具链。

sentences.en: The only thing missing at link time is the GTK4 shared library itself, and -Dgtk-stub covers that, as it builds a tiny stub libgtk-4.so.1 whose exported symbols are all no-ops, links the executable against that, and lets the target’s real GTK4 resolve at runtime instead.
sentences.zh: 链接时唯一缺少的是 GTK4 共享库本身，而 -Dgtk-stub 涵盖了这一点，因为它构建了一个微小的存根 libgtk-4.so.1，其导出的符号都是无操作的，将可执行文件链接到该共享库，并让目标的真实 GTK4 在运行时解析。

sentences.en: The release workflow uses this to produce binaries for x86_64, aarch64, armv7, riscv64, powerpc64le, i386, loongarch64 and s390x from one machine, none of which has GTK4 installed for the other seven.
sentences.zh: 发布工作流程使用它从一台机器上生成 x86_64、aarch64、armv7、riscv64、powerpc64le、i386、loongarch64 和 s390x 的二进制文件，其中没有一台机器为其他七台机器安装了 GTK4。

blocks.html_en: Note: ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t grab the keyboard as other askpass implementations normally would. The GTK3 helper calls gdk_seat_grab so another client can’t read the passphrase as you type it, but from what I see, GTK4 dropped that interface and I believe that Wayland doesn’t let a client grab the keyboard at all, so there is no portable way to do it without X11. Hence the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER and GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER variables also have no effect.

sentences.en: Note: ssh-askpass-zigtk doesn’t grab the keyboard as other askpass implementations normally would.
sentences.zh: 注意：ssh-askpass-zigtk 不会像其他 Askpass 实现通常那样抓取键盘。

sentences.en: The GTK3 helper calls gdk_seat_grab so another client can’t read the passphrase as you type it, but from what I see, GTK4 dropped that interface and I believe that Wayland doesn’t let a client grab the keyboard at all, so there is no portable way to do it without X11.
sentences.zh: GTK3 帮助程序调用 gdk_seat_grab，以便其他客户端无法在您键入密码时读取密码，但从我看来，GTK4 放弃了该界面，并且我相信 Wayland 根本不允许客户端抓取键盘，因此没有 X11 就没有可移植的方法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Hence the GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER and GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER variables also have no effect.
sentences.zh: 因此，GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER 和 GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER 变量也不起作用。

我在笔记本电脑上运行强化的 Gentoo，大多数时候我从不碰 ssh-askpass，因为我在大多数系统中使用 -sk 密钥。 不过，有一类情况我确实需要它，即程序需要常规 ED25519 密钥的 SSH 密钥密码，但没有终端可以读取它。 通常的情况是 go get，或者一般的 go 工具链，在没有 TTY 的情况下运行的构建过程中通过 SSH 获取私有模块。 OpenSSH 无法在管道上进行提示，因此它会运行 SSH_ASKPASS 指向的任何内容，并将密码提示放在窗口中。 多年来我没有为此安装任何东西，并且必须解决这些情况。 主要原因是 Gentoo 的 Portage 提供的功能：

这就是我放弃打包选项的地方。 即使抛开X11问题，​​这些都最多使用GTK2或GTK3。 然而，碰巧的是，我长期以来一直想用 GTK4 构建一些东西，所以我没有修补现有的实现之一（无论如何大部分都是 C 语言），而是用 Zig 0.16 和 GTK4 编写了自己的实现，并将其命名为 ssh-askpass-zigtk。

避免X11

GTK 帮助程序在我的系统上崩溃的原因是标头。 调用 GTK 的标准方法包括 GTK4 标头，它会引入 GDK，并且 GDK 在大多数安装中仍然附带 gdk/gdkx.h，因此无论您是否需要，都会出现 X11 标头。 Zig 的 @cImport 是调用 C 库的明显方法，也会做同样的事情，因为它准确地提取了这些标头。 所以 ssh-askpass-zigtk 不会 @cImport 任何东西。 src/gtk.zig 声明了程序手动调用的三十多个 GTK 和 GLib 函数，作为简单的 extern 原型：

pub const Widget = opaque {};

pub extern fn gtk_window_new() *Widget;
pub extern fn gtk_password_entry_new() *Widget;
pub extern fn gtk_editable_get_text(editable: *Widget) [*:0]const u8;
pub extern fn gtk_button_new_with_label(label: [*:0]const u8) *Widget;

该文件中没有任何内容命名 gdk/gdkx.h 或 X11/Xlib.h 中的符号，因此编译器永远不会看到 X 标头，并且二进制文件会针对未使用 X11 编译的 GTK4 进行构建和运行。 它需要的一个 X 相邻值（Escape 键符号）被硬编码为 0xff1b，而不是从 gdk/gdkkeysyms.h 中提取。

GTK 构建于 GObject 之上，它通过将父结构体作为子结构体的第一个成员来实现单继承，因此窗口、框、标签、密码条目和按钮都与 ABI 边界处的 GtkWidget * 布局兼容。 在 Zig 方面，一个不透明的 {} 类型代表所有这些，并且每个 widget 函数都接受并返回相同的 *Widget，没有包装器类型的层次结构来对 C ABI 已经扁平化的东西进行建模。

不涉及 GTK 的部分，即 SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT 到对话框类型的映射以及 GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_*_COLOR 变量的解析，位于 src/root.zig 中并进行了单元测试，因此它们在 zig 构建测试下运行，没有显示，也根本没有 GTK。 由于 GTK4 删除了 gtk_widget_modify_fg 和 _bg，因此重新着色需要通过一个小型 CSS 提供程序。

交叉编译

由于绑定是手写的 extern，并且没有 GTK 标头进入构建，因此 Zig 可以为任何 Linux 架构交叉编译二进制文件，而无需该目标的 GTK4 工具链。 链接时唯一缺少的是 GTK4 共享库本身，而 -Dgtk-stub 涵盖了这一点，因为它构建了一个微小的存根 libgtk-4.so.1，其导出的符号都是无操作的，将可执行文件链接到该共享库，并让目标的真实 GTK4 在运行时解析。 发布工作流程使用它从一台机器上生成 x86_64、aarch64、armv7、riscv64、powerpc64le、i386、loongarch64 和 s390x 的二进制文件，其中没有一台机器为其他七台机器安装了 GTK4。

注意：ssh-askpass-zigtk 不会像其他 Askpass 实现通常那样抓取键盘。 GTK3 帮助程序调用 gdk_seat_grab，以便其他客户端无法在您键入密码时读取密码，但从我看来，GTK4 放弃了该界面，并且我相信 Wayland 根本不允许客户端抓取键盘，因此没有 X11 就没有可移植的方法来做到这一点。 因此，GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_SERVER 和 GNOME_SSH_ASKPASS_GRAB_POINTER 变量也不起作用。

代码位于 tty.fail 上并镜像到 GitHub，其中每个标记版本都针对每个架构提供了预构建的 Linux 二进制文件。 要使用它，请将二进制文件放在 PATH 中的某个位置，并将 SSH_ASKPASS 指向它。 对于一个终端，这意味着 ~/.profile 或 shell 的启动文件中有两行（例如，对于我的 Zsh 用户同伴来说是 ~/.zshrc）：

export SSH_ASKPASS=~/.local/bin/ssh-askpass-zigtk
export SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer

从 OpenSSH 8.4 开始，SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=prefer 告诉 OpenSSH 只要存在图形会话，即使终端可用，也使用该对话框。 在 systemd 用户会话上，相同的两个变量以带有绝对路径的纯 KEY=VALUE 行形式放入 ~/.config/environment.d/ssh-askpass.conf 中，因为该文件既不扩展也不运行 shell。 注销并重新登录，下一个需要密码短语而无需终端的 ssh-add、git pull 或 go get 会出现对话框。
